name: Ellerbrück
basis: Drawn only from public-domain folk and fairy tales: the Brothers Grimm (1812-1857 editions of the Kinder- und Hausmärchen, and Deutsche Sagen), Perrault (1697), Andersen (1835-1872) and older European folklore, all long out of copyright. Nothing from Disney or any modern adaptation; the town and its people are invented.
summary: A walled market town where a stone bridge crosses the river Eller, with a small castle on the hill, a mill, guild lanes, goose meadows and a great dark forest beyond the fields, where people still tell the old tales about their neighbours.

curated-2026-10.title: Ellerbrück quarters, places and trades written for Prospero Dungeon
curated-2026-10.note: An original town for fiction. Tale lore comes only from public-domain texts: Grimm's Rumpelstiltskin, Elves and the Shoemaker, Hansel and Gretel, Bremen Town Musicians, Rapunzel, Goose Girl, Mother Holle, Little Red Cap, Brave Little Tailor, Sweet Porridge, Table-Be-Set, Clever Elsie, Hans in Luck, Fisherman and His Wife, Three Golden Hairs, Briar Rose, Aschenputtel, Golden Goose, Wolf and Seven Kids; the Hamelin ratcatcher (Deutsche Sagen, 1816); Perrault's Little Thumb and Puss in Boots (1697); Andersen's Princess and the Pea (1835). Nothing from Disney or later adaptations. Streets, inns and townsfolk are invented on the pattern of small Hessian towns; coordinates are a fixed anchor in northern Hesse. Rents are rough weekly sums in groschen. Climate is approximate Kassel-area averages, rounded.

neighborhoods.name: Am Markt
neighborhoods.summary: The cobbled market square at the heart of the town, with the town hall, the fountain, the best inn and the stalls on market days.

neighborhoods.name: Schlossberg
neighborhoods.summary: The hill above the market with the Count's small castle, its gardens, its kitchens and the houses of the court officials.

neighborhoods.name: Schustergasse
neighborhoods.summary: The cobblers' and tailors' lane, narrow and crooked, with workshops on the ground floor and families above.

neighborhoods.name: Bäckergasse
neighborhoods.summary: The bakers' street behind the market, warm and smelling of bread from before dawn, with the common bakehouse and the porridge kitchen.

neighborhoods.name: Weberviertel
neighborhoods.summary: The spinners' and weavers' quarter by the north wall, loud with looms by day and full of spinning rooms on winter nights.

neighborhoods.name: St. Martin's Kirchhof
neighborhoods.summary: The quiet close around St. Martin's church and the convent of St. Clare, with the churchyard, the parsonage and the convent school.

neighborhoods.name: Mühlbach
neighborhoods.summary: The mill on the stream below the west wall, with its pond, weir and a cluster of millers' and carters' cottages.

neighborhoods.name: Am Fährhaus
neighborhoods.summary: The riverbank below the bridge where the ferry crosses, with fishermen's huts, drying nets and the Flounder tavern.

neighborhoods.name: Gerberviertel
neighborhoods.summary: The tanners' quarter downstream by the south gate, smelly and cheap, with the bathhouse, the ratcatcher and the cheapest rooms in town.

neighborhoods.name: Gänseanger
neighborhoods.summary: The goose meadow outside the dark east gate, with the cattle market ground, the marksmen's field and the carters' inn.

neighborhoods.name: Gartenvorstadt
neighborhoods.summary: Walled kitchen gardens and orchards outside the north gate, and beyond them the open fields where the old tower stands.

neighborhoods.name: Am Waldrand
neighborhoods.summary: A hamlet of woodcutters and charcoal burners where the fields end and the forest begins, an hour's walk from the market.

neighborhoods.name: Jägerhof
neighborhoods.summary: The Count's hunting lodge and the foresters' houses on the forest road, with trails running off into the deep wood.

neighborhoods.name: Eichdorf
neighborhoods.summary: A farming village of strip fields, geese and a great linden tree, a half hour south of town across the bridge.

transit.name: On foot
transit.summary: Everyone walks: the walls take twenty minutes to go round and the farthest hamlets are an hour out.

transit.name: Carters' wagons
transit.summary: Ox and horse carts haul grain, timber and passengers willing to sit on the load, leaving from the market on market days.

transit.name: Hired horses
transit.summary: Horses can be hired from the Golden Goose by the east gate, and court messengers ride the Count's.

transit.name: The Eller ferry
transit.summary: A rope ferry crosses the Eller below the bridge for carts too heavy for the old stone arches.

transit.name: Mill barges
transit.summary: Flat barges carry flour and hides between the mill, the tanyards and the bridge.

places.name: the Marktplatz
places.summary: The sloping market square in front of the town hall, where news is cried, notices are nailed up and children chase pigeons.

places.name: the Wednesday and Saturday market
places.summary: Stalls of eggs, cheese, cabbages, geese, pots and cloth fill the square twice a week.

places.name: the market fountain
places.summary: A stone basin fed by a spring, where the town draws water and maids trade gossip with full buckets.

places.name: the Ratskeller
places.summary: A vaulted cellar under the town hall serving beer, wine and roast pork to councillors and anyone who can pay.

places.name: Zum Tischlein
places.summary: The best inn in town, whose landlord gets touchy if guests ask whether he ever swapped a magic table for a plain one.

places.name: the Swan apothecary
places.summary: Jars of salves, dried herbs and cough syrups behind a counter on the corner of the square.

places.name: the castle gardens
places.summary: Box hedges, fruit walls and a fountain behind the castle, opened to townsfolk on Sunday afternoons.

places.name: the briar hedge
places.summary: A thick old hedge of wild roses grown over the ruined east wing, which the Count's gardeners are forbidden to cut.

places.name: the castle courtyard
places.summary: The cobbled court inside the gate where petitioners wait, carts unload for the kitchens and the guard changes.

places.name: the castle chapel
places.summary: A small painted chapel where the household hears mass and townsfolk may come in on feast days.

places.name: the castle kitchen garden
places.summary: Rows of cabbages, beans and herbs below the kitchen windows, worked by the royal gardener and his boys.

places.name: the castle lookout
places.summary: A linden-shaded terrace on the castle wall with a view over the roofs, the river and the dark line of the forest.

places.name: the gate kitchen
places.summary: A hatch beside the castle gate where the under-cook sells yesterday's roasts and pies to petitioners, and boxes the scullion's ears if he dozes off.

places.name: Lorenz's shoe shop
places.summary: A cobbler's shop with a pair of huge boots in the window labelled "seven leagues a stride, price on asking".

places.name: the Seven-at-a-Blow tailor
places.summary: A tailor's shop whose owner keeps an embroidered belt over the counter and swears his grandfather earned it.

places.name: Zum Roten Stiefel
places.summary: The Red Boot, a low-beamed tavern where journeymen drink after work and argue about their masters.

places.name: the journeymen's hostel
places.summary: Cheap bunks for travelling journeymen, kept by the guilds, with a long table for soup in the evening.

places.name: the shoemakers' and tailors' guildhall
places.summary: A timber hall where the two guilds meet, test apprentices and hold their dances at Shrovetide.

places.name: Becker's bakery
places.summary: Rye loaves, pretzels and poppy-seed rolls sold through the window from first light.

places.name: the porridge kitchen
places.summary: A widow's kitchen selling bowls of sweet millet porridge from a pot she swears she always tells to stop.

places.name: the gingerbread baker
places.summary: Spiced honey cakes and gingerbread hearts, though the baker refuses outright to build a gingerbread cottage.

places.name: the common bakehouse
places.summary: The town oven where households bring their own dough to bake on Fridays and pay the baker a loaf in twenty.

places.name: the sausage stall
places.summary: Grilled sausages on rye with mustard, sold from a brazier at the market end of the street.

places.name: Zum Krug
places.summary: The Jug, a bakers' alehouse that opens at noon when the ovens cool and closes early.

places.name: the deep well
places.summary: An old well in the weavers' yard where, the story goes, a girl once dropped her spindle and climbed down after it.

places.name: the spinning room
places.summary: A big warm room where women bring their wheels on winter evenings to spin, sing and tell stories by one candle.

places.name: the weavers' yard
places.summary: A courtyard ringed with loom rooms where linen is woven for the market and the castle.

places.name: the bleaching green
places.summary: A meadow inside the wall where linen is spread to whiten in the sun and children are paid to keep the geese off.

places.name: Zur Spindel
places.summary: The Spindle, a weavers' tavern with cheap cider and a fiddler on Saturdays.

places.name: St. Martin's church
places.summary: The town church with its squat tower, painted saints and the bell that rings the hours and the curfew.

places.name: the hazel tree in the churchyard
places.summary: An old hazel on a grave in the churchyard, where girls make wishes and leave a few lentils for the birds.

places.name: the convent of St. Clare
places.summary: A small house of nuns who keep a school, a herb garden and a guest room for women travelling alone.

places.name: the churchyard linden
places.summary: A huge linden with a stone bench around its trunk, where old men sit after mass and the elders once held court.

places.name: the parish library
places.summary: A room over the sacristy with chained books, sermons and an herbal, open to anyone who can read and asks the sexton.

places.name: the sexton's alehouse
places.summary: Beer drawn in the sexton's front room by the lych gate; he no longer climbs the tower after dark, not since a boy who wanted to learn to shudder threw him down the stairs.

places.name: the old mill
places.summary: The undershot mill on the Mühlbach, whose miller once boasted that his daughter could spin straw into gold.

places.name: the millpond
places.summary: A reedy pond above the weir with ducks, a pair of swans and a path round it for an evening walk.

places.name: the millrace path
places.summary: A footpath along the millrace from the west gate to the weir under willows and alders.

places.name: Zum Kater
places.summary: The Tomcat, a millers' tavern named for the youngest son who was left nothing but the mill cat.

places.name: the mill ford
places.summary: Stepping stones across the stream below the mill, where carts splash through and boys catch crayfish.

places.name: the ferry landing
places.summary: The ferry stage under the bridge, where the ferryman pulls his raft across on a rope and grumbles that nobody ever takes the pole.

places.name: the fish stalls
places.summary: Fishermen's wives selling pike, carp, eel and crayfish from tubs on the bank every morning.

places.name: Zum Butt
places.summary: The Flounder, a fishermen's tavern whose landlady is teased that she will want a palace next.

places.name: the bathing meadow
places.summary: A grassy bank and gravel shallows upstream of the ferry where the town swims on hot afternoons.

places.name: the towpath
places.summary: A riverside path along the Eller past fishing huts, willows and the old boundary stones.

places.name: the bathhouse
places.summary: A steam bath with hot tubs and a barber who trims beards, lets blood and knows everyone's business.

places.name: the tanyards
places.summary: Tan pits and drying sheds on the river below the town, kept downstream and downwind for good reason.

places.name: the ratcatcher's house
places.summary: A crooked house with the council's unpaid bill nailed to the door, kept by a ratcatcher with a long memory.

places.name: Zur Laute
places.summary: The Lute, a rough tavern where the town band of four old players has been "about to leave for Bremen" for twenty years.

places.name: the south gate cookshop
places.summary: Lentil soup, blood sausage and black bread for tanners and carters at the cheapest prices in town.

places.name: the goose meadow
places.summary: A long green meadow outside the east gate where the goose girls drive the town's geese every morning.

places.name: the dark gate
places.summary: The deep, dim east gate, with an old carved horse's head over the arch that the goose girls greet as they pass.

places.name: the cattle market ground
places.summary: Pens and hitching rails where cows, pigs, horses and geese are traded on the first Monday of each month.

places.name: the Golden Goose
places.summary: The carters' inn by the east gate, with stabling, a long table and a painted goose on the sign that people swear sticks to fingers.

places.name: the marksmen's field
places.summary: A meadow with crossbow butts and a wooden bird on a pole, where the marksmen's guild shoots on summer Sundays.

places.name: the walled rampion garden
places.summary: A high-walled garden full of rampion and lettuces whose owner sells nothing and lets nobody in.

places.name: the tower in the fields
places.summary: An old stone tower in the fields with one window at the top and no door at all, which nobody claims to own.

places.name: the apothecary's garden
places.summary: Neat beds of sage, chamomile, foxglove and poppies grown for the Swan apothecary's jars.

places.name: the orchard path
places.summary: A path through apple and pear meadows from the north gate out toward the tower.

places.name: the garden tavern
places.summary: Tables under chestnut trees behind a market gardener's house, serving cider, cheese and radishes on summer evenings.

places.name: the woodyard
places.summary: A clearing stacked with cut logs, where the woodcutters split and sell firewood to carters from town.

places.name: the path children are told not to take
places.summary: A narrow track into the deep forest toward an old woman's cottage that local children are warned away from.

places.name: the charcoal kilns
places.summary: Smoking turf-covered mounds tended day and night by the charcoal burners in their huts.

places.name: the forest spring
places.summary: A cold spring under beeches at the edge of the wood, a favourite place to rest on the way back with firewood.

places.name: the woodcutters' alehouse
places.summary: A one-room alehouse with a bench outside, where woodcutters drink thin beer and talk about hard winters.

places.name: the hunting lodge inn
places.summary: The Count's old hunting lodge, now partly an inn serving venison and wild-mushroom stew to travellers on the forest road.

places.name: the forest road path
places.summary: The marked path through the wood to the next village, where every parent says to keep to the path and not stop to pick flowers.

places.name: the high seat
places.summary: A wooden hunting stand on the edge of a clearing where deer come out at dusk.

places.name: the mushroom woods
places.summary: Beech and oak woods where townsfolk go for mushrooms, bilberries and beechnuts in late summer and autumn.

places.name: the wayside shrine
places.summary: A painted shrine to St. Hubert on the forest road, where hunters leave a sprig of oak.

places.name: the dancing linden
places.summary: A great linden on the village green with a wooden floor built into its lower branches for dancing on feast days.

places.name: the village green
places.summary: Common grass with a pond for the geese, a pump and a bench for the old men.

places.name: the cider press
places.summary: A farmhouse press that sells new cider and onion tart at long tables in autumn.

places.name: Eichdorf chapel
places.summary: A plain stone chapel with a wooden bell tower, served by the curate from town every other Sunday.

places.name: the field path
places.summary: A path between strips of rye, flax and cabbages from the village back to the bridge.

careers.name: Woodcutter
careers.summary: Felling and splitting timber at the forest edge and selling firewood to carters from town.

careers.name: Charcoal burner
careers.summary: Building and tending the smoking kilns in the woods day and night for the smiths' charcoal.

careers.name: Miller
careers.summary: Grinding grain at the Mühlbach mill and taking a share of every sack as toll.

careers.name: Goose girl
careers.summary: Driving the town's geese out through the dark gate to the meadow at dawn and home again at dusk.

careers.name: Shoemaker
careers.summary: Cutting and stitching shoes and boots in a Schustergasse workshop, from the last to the finished pair.

careers.name: Tailor
careers.summary: Cutting cloth, fitting customers and sewing coats and gowns, cross-legged on the workbench.

careers.name: Baker
careers.summary: Firing the oven before dawn for rye loaves, rolls and pretzels, by the town's weight rules.

careers.name: Spinner
careers.summary: Spinning flax and wool at home or in the spinning room, paid by the skein.

careers.name: Weaver
careers.summary: Weaving linen on a loom in the Weberviertel for merchants and the castle.

careers.name: Huntsman
careers.summary: Keeping the Count's game, culling deer and boar, and walking the forest road.

careers.name: Ferryman
careers.summary: Pulling the rope ferry across the Eller for carts, cattle and walkers, in all weathers.

careers.name: Fisher
careers.summary: Setting nets and eel traps on the Eller and selling the catch from tubs on the bank.

careers.name: Innkeeper's hand
careers.summary: Cooking, serving, making beds and stabling horses at one of the town's inns.

careers.name: Apothecary
careers.summary: Making salves, syrups and powders at the Swan apothecary and advising on coughs and fevers.

careers.name: Royal gardener
careers.summary: Keeping the castle's hedges, fruit walls and kitchen beds, and never cutting the briar hedge.

careers.name: Castle servant
careers.summary: Kitchen, laundry or chamber work in the Count's household, paid in wages, food and a livery coat.

careers.name: Tanner
careers.summary: Scraping hides and working the tan pits in the Gerberviertel.

careers.name: Ratcatcher
careers.summary: Trapping rats in cellars, granaries and the mill, and reminding the council what it owes.

careers.name: Town musician
careers.summary: Playing fiddle, horn or drum at weddings, dances and taverns as one of the town band.

careers.name: Carter
careers.summary: Driving ox and horse wagons of grain, timber and flour between the forest, the mill and the market.

careers.name: Market gardener
careers.summary: Growing cabbages, lettuces, onions and herbs in the Gartenvorstadt for the market.

careers.name: Convent schoolteacher
careers.summary: Teaching girls and small boys to read, count and sew at the convent of St. Clare.

employers.name: the Count's household
employers.summary: The steward's household that runs the castle's kitchens, laundry, chambers and stables.

employers.name: the castle gardens
employers.summary: The head gardener and his boys, who keep the castle gardens and kitchen beds.

employers.name: the Count's forest office
employers.summary: The head forester's office at the hunting lodge, which licenses woodcutting and keeps the game.

employers.name: the hunting lodge inn
employers.summary: The inn in the old lodge on the forest road.

employers.name: the Mühlbach mill
employers.summary: The town's water mill, leased from the Count to the master miller and his family.

employers.name: Zum Tischlein
employers.summary: The best inn on the market square, with kitchens, rooms and stabling.

employers.name: the Golden Goose
employers.summary: The carters' inn by the east gate, with stabling and horses for hire.

employers.name: the shoemakers' and tailors' guild
employers.summary: The two craft guilds of Schustergasse and their masters' workshops.

employers.name: the weavers' guild
employers.summary: The guild of the Weberviertel's weavers, who also put out flax to spinners.

employers.name: the bakers of Bäckergasse
employers.summary: Four family bakeries and the common bakehouse under the bakers' guild.

employers.name: the Swan apothecary
employers.summary: The town's only apothecary, with a shop on the square and a garden outside the north gate.

employers.name: the Eller ferry and fishery
employers.summary: The ferry rights and fishing leases on the Eller, held from the town council.

employers.name: the Gerberviertel tanyards
employers.summary: Three family tanyards on the river below the south gate.

employers.name: the town council
employers.summary: The mayor and council in the town hall, who pay the goose girls, the band and, in theory, the ratcatcher.

employers.name: the convent of St. Clare
employers.summary: The nuns' house by St. Martin's, which runs the school and the herb garden.

employers.name: the Eichdorf farms
employers.summary: The village's farmers, who hire hands for haymaking and harvest and send geese to market.

career_hubs.name: The castle and the forest
career_hubs.summary: The Count's household, gardens and forest office employ servants, gardeners, huntsmen and woodcutters.

career_hubs.name: The guild lanes
career_hubs.summary: Workshops, bakeries, inns and shops of the town's guilds inside the walls.

career_hubs.name: The river and the fields
career_hubs.summary: The mill, ferry, tanyards, goose meadow and farms along the Eller.

climate.summary: Approximate central-German weather: cold, grey winters with frost and some snow, late springs, warm summers with thunderstorms, and misty autumns.

months.note: Cold; frost and the odd snowfall.
Grey and raw; snow lies in the forest.
Changeable; orchards in blossom late in the month.
Mild and green; geese out on the meadow.
Warmest month; swimming in the Eller.
Warm; rye harvest in the fields.
Cool and misty; leaves turn in the forest.
Damp and dark early; first frosts.
Cold and short days; snow some years.

annual_events.name: Star singers
annual_events.summary: Children in paper crowns carry a star from door to door at Epiphany, singing and chalking a blessing over each lintel.

annual_events.name: Fastnacht
annual_events.summary: The guilds hold dances and the journeymen parade in masks before Lent begins.

annual_events.name: Walpurgis night
annual_events.summary: Bonfires on the hills and a racket of pots and whips to drive off witches on the last night of April.

annual_events.name: May Day
annual_events.summary: Young people bring in birch boughs at dawn and dance round the maypole and the linden on Eichdorf green.

annual_events.name: The marksmen's festival
annual_events.summary: A week of crossbow shooting at a wooden bird, with a parade, a fair and a marksman king crowned for the year.

annual_events.name: Midsummer fires
annual_events.summary: Bonfires on the riverbank on St. John's Eve, with couples jumping the embers and wreaths floated on the Eller.

annual_events.name: Harvest home
annual_events.summary: The last sheaf is tied into a figure and carried to the farm on a wagon, followed by a supper and dancing.

annual_events.name: Kirmes
annual_events.summary: The church-dedication fair: booths, swings, roast ox and three days of dancing on the market square.

annual_events.name: Harvest thanksgiving
annual_events.summary: A harvest crown of grain and apples is hung in St. Martin's and the bread of the year is blessed.

annual_events.name: Cider pressing
annual_events.summary: Families bring windfalls to the press and drink the new cider with onion tart at long tables.

annual_events.name: Martinmas lanterns
annual_events.summary: Children carry paper lanterns through the streets singing St. Martin's songs, and every family that can afford one eats goose.

annual_events.name: St. Nicholas's Eve
annual_events.summary: Children put out their shoes and find nuts, apples and gingerbread from the bakers in them in the morning.

annual_events.name: The Christmas market
annual_events.summary: Through Advent the square fills with booths of gingerbread, toys, candles and hot spiced wine.

annual_events.name: Spinning room season
annual_events.summary: From Martinmas to Candlemas the spinning rooms are full every evening of wheels, songs and long stories.

local_color.name: The miller's boast
local_color.summary: When someone oversells a child or an apprentice, people say "careful, or they'll have to spin straw into gold", after the old miller of Mühlbach.

local_color.name: "The elves finished it"
local_color.summary: Shoemakers who find work done that nobody admits to doing say the elves came in the night, and some leave out a small suit of clothes at Christmas just in case.

local_color.name: Seven-league boots
local_color.summary: Lorenz the cobbler keeps a pair of enormous boots in his window as a joke and quotes an absurd price to anyone who asks.

local_color.name: "Keep to the path"
local_color.summary: Every child sent through the wood is told to keep to the path, not stop to pick flowers and not talk to strangers, wolves especially.

local_color.name: The cottage in the wood
local_color.summary: Children are warned off the track to an old woman's cottage deep in the forest, and told never to eat anything they find there.

local_color.name: The band that never got to Bremen
local_color.summary: The town band of four old players, a braying horn, a fiddle, a growling bass and a crowing tenor, has been leaving for Bremen any day now for twenty years.

local_color.name: The unpaid ratcatcher
local_color.summary: The council still owes the ratcatcher for clearing the granaries, he reminds them at every meeting, and mothers keep children indoors whenever he takes out his pipe.

local_color.name: The tower with no door
local_color.summary: Nobody knows who built the tower in the fields; children dare each other to call up to the window, and the market gardeners give the walled rampion garden next to it a wide berth.

local_color.name: Frau Holle is shaking her beds
local_color.summary: When it snows, people say Mother Holle is shaking out her feather beds, and a hard-working girl is called a "gold girl".

local_color.name: Greeting the horse over the gate
local_color.summary: Goose girls say good morning to the carved horse's head over the dark gate every day, after the goose girl of the old story.

local_color.name: "Little pot, stop!"
local_color.summary: Said when anything runs on too long, from the tale of the sweet porridge pot that flooded a town because nobody knew the word to stop it.

local_color.name: Sweet millet porridge
local_color.summary: Millet boiled in milk with honey and a pinch of cinnamon, the everyday breakfast for children and the poor.

local_color.name: "Seven at one blow"
local_color.summary: A boast that turns out smaller than it sounds, after the little tailor whose seven were flies.

local_color.name: A Hans-in-luck trade
local_color.summary: Swapping something good for something worse and feeling pleased about it, like Hans who traded a lump of gold down to nothing on his way home.

local_color.name: A Clever Elsie
local_color.summary: Someone who worries about troubles that have not happened yet, after the girl who wept in the cellar over a child she did not have.

local_color.name: "Like Ilsebill"
local_color.summary: Said of anyone never satisfied with what they have, after the fisherman's wife who kept asking the flounder for more.

local_color.name: The pea under the mattress
local_color.summary: A fussy guest is said to feel a pea through twenty mattresses, and the landlord of Zum Tischlein keeps a dried pea in a dish as a joke.

local_color.name: Martinmas goose
local_color.summary: Roast goose with red cabbage and dumplings on St. Martin's day, the year's one goose for families who can manage it.

local_color.name: Gingerbread
local_color.summary: Honey-and-spice cakes baked from Advent, sold as hearts and figures, though the baker will not make cottages.

local_color.name: "Show me your paw"
local_color.summary: What parents teach children to say before opening the door to a stranger, from the goat and the seven young kids.

holidays.name: New Year's Day
holidays.summary: The new year is rung in from St. Martin's tower and neighbours call with good wishes.

holidays.name: Epiphany
holidays.summary: Twelfth Day, when the star singers go round and the Christmas greenery comes down.

holidays.name: Candlemas
holidays.summary: Candles are blessed at St. Martin's and the spinning-room season ends.

holidays.name: Fastnacht
holidays.summary: The last day before Lent, with doughnuts, masks and guild dances.

holidays.name: Good Friday
holidays.summary: A quiet day of fasting; the bells are silent until Easter.

holidays.name: Easter Sunday
holidays.summary: Coloured eggs, new clothes and the first lamb of the year after mass.

holidays.name: Easter Monday
holidays.summary: A day off for walking out to the villages and egg-rolling on the meadows.

holidays.name: Walpurgis night
holidays.summary: Bonfires and noise to drive off witches on the eve of May.

holidays.name: May Day
holidays.summary: Birch boughs on the doors and dancing round the maypole.

holidays.name: Ascension Day
holidays.summary: A holiday for walking the town bounds and drinking in the garden taverns.

holidays.name: Whit Monday
holidays.summary: Shops shut, the guilds walk out to the woods and the cattle go up to summer grazing.

holidays.name: St. John's Day
holidays.summary: Midsummer: bonfires on the eve and herbs gathered at dawn.

holidays.name: Harvest thanksgiving
holidays.summary: The harvest crown at St. Martin's on the first Sunday of October.

holidays.name: All Souls' Day
holidays.summary: Graves are tidied and candles lit in the churchyard.

holidays.name: Martinmas
holidays.summary: Lantern processions, roast goose, and rents and wages due.

holidays.name: St. Nicholas's Day
holidays.summary: Children find nuts and gingerbread in their shoes.

holidays.name: Christmas Eve
holidays.summary: Shops close at noon and families gather for carp and the midnight mass.

holidays.name: Christmas Day
holidays.summary: Mass, a goose or a ham, and no work in the fields.

holidays.name: St. Stephen's Day
holidays.summary: The second day of Christmas, for visiting and riding out the horses.
